newsitem.title: BOSNIA: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA PROMOTES BOSNIA'S FIRST POST-WAR SKI RACE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA PROMOTES BOSNIA'S FIRST POST-WAR SKI RACE.

text.p: Italian Alpine skiing champion Alberto Tomba travelled to Bosnia on Monday to promote the first peacetime slalom race in Sarajevo where ski resorts were ripped apart during the 3-1/2 year war.
Tomba said the "Slalom of Peace" on Mount Bjelasnica outside Sarajevo would be held on December 23 and pledged to bring 100 of the world's top skiers for the event.
"With this competition, I want to show the world what has happened here," Tomba told reporters.
Tomba, a double Olympic gold medallist and five times world champion, took a walking tour of ski slopes on Mount Bjelasnica where he competed in the World Cup in 1987.

Ten years on, the mountain offered a shockingly different scene, with skeletons of ski lifts strewn on the mountain and rubble where hotels were burned to the ground by the Bosnian Serb army in the summer of 1993.
"I've seen the pictures on TV but it cannot be compared with what you see when you come here," Tomba said.
Since the Bosnian war ended with a peace accord in November 1995, only one ski lift has been repaired on Mount Bjelasnica, 33 kms south-east of Sarajevo.
Tomba said he wanted to help Sarajevo, which hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics, to bid for the 2006 Games. "We have enough time and we can succeed in that," he said.

Tomba, who helped to organise free training in Italy for numerous young skiers from Bosnia during the 1992-1995 war, attracted a crowd of children who flocked around him as he inspected Sarajevo's Olympic ski slopes.
